IsAllowed.maps_to: no counterpart; `Relic` declares no `is_allowed` member at all
IsAllowed.issue: See guard G1 -- pool eligibility has no sim concept. FrozenEgg.cs:16-19 returns RelicModel.IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest(runState) = `TotalFloor < 41` (RelicModel.cs:452-456), so the game stops offering Frozen Egg from the Act 3 treasure chest onward. Executed (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b06.py b06-isallowed`): `'is_allowed' in dir(Relic)` is False, the relic is Rare in the transcribed grab bag, RunState tracks total_floor, and the only per-pull filters in the pull path are is_allowed_in_shops checks (run.py:592, 614, 626). LIVE.

TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate.issue: Rollup of guards G2 and G4 per binding rule 4. The effect matches -- EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards(cardRewards, CardType.Power, this) (EggRelicHelper.cs:10-22) upgrades every reward option of the matching type that IsUpgradable, and _eggs.py:34-42 does the same through `_applies` -- but the `options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoHookUpgrades)` bail (FrozenEgg.cs:27-30) has no sim counterpart (G2), and the Late phase is collapsed into the sim's single flat pass (G4).

ModifyMerchantCardCreationResults.rationale: FrozenEgg.cs:35-41 delegates to the same EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards with the same card type and no flags check, and _eggs.py:44-45 delegates to the same `modify_card_reward_options` body. The owner guard is N1 (waived). MerchantCardEntry computes the price from the modified card on both sides because the hook runs before pricing (relics/base.py:177-180 says so).

TryModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck.rationale: FrozenEgg.cs:43-61 checks owner, `card.Type != CardType.Power`, `!card.IsUpgradable`, then CloneCards the card, upgrades the CLONE and returns it as `newCard`; _eggs.py:47-51 checks the same two card conditions through `_applies` and upgrades the card IN PLACE, returning the same object. Executed (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): an Inflame added to the deck comes out at upgrade_level 1 and is the same object that was passed in. Verdicted a divergence rather than a gap under binding rule 2 because the observable -- the deck's (id, upgrade_level) contents, which conformance/runner.py compares -- is identical, and a freshly created card entering the deck carries no per-instance state for CloneCard to preserve. It is NOT waived and NOT faithful: the identity difference is real, and see guard G3 for the one shape where it would matter.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoHookUpgrades) -> return false` (FrozenEgg.cs:27-30) has no sim counterpart
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the flag lets a card-creation call opt out of relic-driven upgrades; CardFactory also honours a sibling NoModifyHooks flag that skips the reward-options hooks entirely (CardFactory.cs:104). The sim has no card-creation-options object and no flags concept -- executed: `'CardCreationFlags' in dir(sts2_rl.hooks)` is False (`py tools/audit/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`), and rewards.py's generator passes a plain `modify_hooks` boolean instead. So a sim caller that wants un-upgraded options can suppress the whole hook loop but cannot suppress only the upgrade half. DORMANT: no ported sim call site asks for NoHookUpgrades, because the flag has no representation to ask with. Porting any C# effect that creates cards WithFlags(NoHookUpgrades) -- the shape exists in the source's card-generation callers -- makes it live, and it would land silently: the sim would upgrade a Power the game left alone. Recorded on this record and not on _eggs.py because the flag check lives in FrozenEgg.cs, not in the shared helper.

guards.what: G3: the sim upgrades the ORIGINAL card object where C# substitutes an upgraded CloneCard (FrozenEgg.cs:58-59; EggRelicHelper.cs:17-19)
guards.issue: PROMPT.md bug class 17 at the egg relics' two sites. CardScope.CloneCard -> ClonePreservingMutability (CardModel.cs:2168-2179) carries upgrade level, enchantment, affliction, keyword edits and local energy-cost modifiers; the sim has no clone helper at all (sweep E). Same mechanism, same verdict as audits/relic/burning_sticks.json G3 -- binding rule 3. DORMANT here, and for a reason worth stating precisely: because the sim MUTATES rather than rebuilds, it does not lose per-instance state the way sweep E's five rebuild sites do -- the divergence is the reverse, that the game keeps the un-upgraded ORIGINAL alive and adds a new model. That matters only where something holds a reference to the pre-modification card: `CardCreationResult.ModifyCard(newCard, source)` records the original for the reward screen's 'modified by' display (presentation), and a merchant entry re-reads its card. The concrete thing that would make it live is a sim effect that keeps a handle on a card across add_card -- e.g. a relic reacting to after_card_added_to_deck and comparing identity with the offered option. _eggs.py:19 states the in-place choice deliberately, which is why this is filed as the class-17 gap rather than as a port error.

guards.what: G4 (DORMANT): the hook is TryModifyCardRewardOptions**Late** and the sim's modify_card_reward_options is a single flat pass
guards.issue: audits/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G3 (missing phase passes) at a site step 28 names by hook (TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate, Hook.cs:1988); one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3. Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions (Hook.cs:1445-1468) runs the plain pass over every listener and THEN the Late pass over every listener; rewards.py:298-301 runs one loop over run.relics. DORMANT: the ported relics that modify reward options either upgrade (the three eggs, Silver Crucible) or enchant (Silken Tress, Glitter, and Fresnel Lens once implemented), and the two families commute -- an upgraded card is still Glam-eligible and vice versa, since EnchantmentModel.CanEnchant does not read the upgrade level (EnchantmentModel.cs:273-294). Porting a plain-phase listener whose decision depends on the upgrade level (a rarity- or cost-reading option filter is the obvious shape) makes it live.

guards.what: N2: the card TYPE -- sts2's Frozen Egg upgrades POWERS, not Skills
guards.rationale: FrozenEgg.cs:31, 39 and 50 all name CardType.Power, and frozen_egg.py:15 sets CARD_TYPE = CardType.POWER. Recorded deliberately because the mapping differs from sts1 (in sts2 Toxic is Skill, Frozen is Power, Molten is Attack) and relics/_eggs.py:1-4 flags it as a known trap.

guards.what: N3: `card.IsUpgradable` is checked on all three paths in C#; the sim checks `card.is_upgradable` inside `_applies` (relics/_eggs.py:35)
guards.rationale: IsUpgradable is `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-789), mirrored by Card.is_upgradable, so PROMPT.md bug class 14 is closed at all three sites -- the eggs never call the unguarded Card.upgrade() on a max_upgrade_level 0 card. Sweep D reached the same conclusion for _eggs.py:39 and :47 by a different route (every level-0 card is Curse/Status/Quest, which the type filter already excludes), so the site is doubly guarded.

guards.what: N4: EggRelic.ONLY_UNUPGRADED = False for Frozen Egg (relics/_eggs.py:30-32, 37)
guards.rationale: MoltenEgg.cs alone refuses an already-upgraded card; FrozenEgg.cs:54 checks only IsUpgradable, so a Power with MaxUpgradeLevel > 1 keeps being bumped. The shared base's flag is left off for this relic, which matches. (Census: no ported card has max_upgrade_level above 1, so the two behaviours coincide today -- the flag is correct rather than merely harmless.)
